questions.stem: Concerning gametogenesis, indicate the correct answer(s):
options: The gonad's only function is gamete production
Cryptorchid testes produce no spermatozoa and testosterone production is blocked
Spermatozoa result from the transformation, without mitosis, of spermatids
In women, the differentiation stage is absent from gametogenesis
questions.explanation: No official answer key for this exam — answers worked out from the course. Cryptorchid testes still secrete testosterone; in women there is no equivalent of spermiogenesis.

questions.stem: Concerning the Sertoli cell, tick the correct answer(s):
options: It phagocytoses the residues of spermiogenesis
It rests on the basement membrane of the seminiferous tubule
It does not take part in regulating spermatogenesis
questions.explanation: No official key — Sertoli cells are stimulated by FSH (Leydig cells by LH).

questions.stem: What is the role of Sertoli cells in spermatogenesis?
options: Nutrition and support of germ cells
Transport of spermatozoa to the epididymis
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: How many cell divisions are needed (from the primary spermatocyte) to form a mature spermatozoon?
questions.explanation: No official key — the two meiotic divisions; spermiogenesis is a transformation without division.

questions.stem: Where does the differentiation of the spermatozoon (spermiogenesis) take place in men?
questions.explanation: No official key — spermiogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules; the epididymis is where spermatozoa mature.

questions.stem: About the 1st week of embryonic development:
options: The zygote is surrounded by the zona pellucida throughout the whole 1st week
During segmentation, the egg does not (or barely) increase in volume because it is surrounded by the zona pellucida
questions.explanation: No official key — the blastocyst hatches from the zona around day 5–6; the blastocoel forms before implantation.

questions.stem: Among the following elements, which enter into the constitution of the chorionic plate?
questions.explanation: No official key — the chorionic plate = extra-embryonic mesoderm + (cyto/syncytio)trophoblast. Heuser's membrane lines the primary yolk sac.

questions.stem: Which process marks the beginning of gastrulation?
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Which crucial structure forms during gastrulation and induces the neural tube?
questions.explanation: No official key — the notochord (axial mesoblast).

questions.stem: About the allantoic diverticulum:
options: It designates a diverticulum that sinks into the embryonic connecting stalk
It only appears at the beginning of the 4th week
It is an endoblastic invagination at the caudal pole of the embryo
It induces the appearance of primordial gonocytes
questions.explanation: No official key — it appears around day 16 (3rd week).

questions.stem: Among the following statements about the amniotic cavity, which is (are) correct?
options: It forms at the beginning of the 2nd week of development
The amnion originates from the syncytiotrophoblast
It appears in the 4th week and contributes to embryonic delimitation
Amniocentesis is a puncture of the amniotic fluid during pregnancy
questions.explanation: No official key — amnioblasts come from the epiblast.

questions.stem: At the start of metamerization, around day 23, the paraxial mesoblast will consist of:
questions.explanation: No official key — first pairs around day 20, about 3 pairs per day.

questions.stem: Among the statements about the intermediate mesoblast, which is (are) correct?
options: The pronephros is represented by functional urinary structures
The mesonephros is a transient urinary structure
The metanephros is at the origin of the urogenital tracts
The metanephros gives rise to the primordium of the definitive kidney
questions.explanation: No official key — the human pronephros is never functional.

questions.stem: Which of the statements below concern the 4th week of embryonic development?
options: Mesencephalic and cervical flexures, head flexed toward the umbilical cord
Closure of the anterior then posterior neuropore
Individualization of the embryo from its annexes
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: The cephalic part of the neural tube gives 3 primary vesicles; in cranio-caudal order we observe:
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: What term describes the process by which ectodermal (epiblast) cells migrate inward to form the mesoblast?
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Which structure is formed by delimitation (folding) and gives rise to internal organs?
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Among the following elements, which derive(s) from the mesoblast?
questions.explanation: No official key — spinal cord and placodes are ectodermal; pancreas is endodermal.

questions.stem: Among the following statements about the pairs of somites, which is (are) correct?
options: They lie on either side of the notochord
They lie on either side of the neural plate
They establish the metameric organization of the body
They appear in pairs in the posterior zone of the embryo's body
questions.explanation: No official key — they appear first in the occipital region and progress caudally.

questions.stem: About stem cells, which assertion(s) is (are) correct?
options: It is a cell capable of differentiating into different cell types
It is found in the developing embryo
It is found in the circulating blood of the body
questions.explanation: No official key — hematopoietic stem cells circulate in small numbers.

questions.stem: Concerning cell differentiation:
options: It is the process by which cells specialize into a cell type identifiable by its own morphological characteristics
A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell
A differentiated cell is characterized by a total loss of mitotic power
The differentiated state is stable but reversible
questions.explanation: No official key — many differentiated cells can still divide.

questions.stem: Among the following statements about dizygotic twins, which is (are) correct?
options: All these twins are dichorionic diamniotic
They always have a different genetic makeup
Their separation occurs very early (at the 2-blastomere stage)
questions.explanation: No official key — dizygotic twins make up about 2/3 of twin cases and come from two eggs, so there is no separation.

questions.stem: The plate (figure) shows cases of twinning. Indicate the correct statement(s); these are:
options: The separation took place at the inner cell mass (embryonic button) stage
The 1st case (A) on the plate represents pygopagus twins
questions.explanation: No official key — conjoined twins come from an incomplete late split of the embryonic disc (monochorionic monoamniotic). Case A is joined at the thorax/abdomen, not the buttocks.

questions.stem: About the diagram (figure), indicate the correct answer(s):
options: It is a phenomenon characteristic of the 2nd week of development
It is the beginning of blastocyst adhesion to the endometrium
It is the formation of the secondary yolk sac (lecithocele)
questions.explanation: No official key — the primary yolk sac is pinched off as an exocoelomic cyst.

questions.stem: Rank the placental villi shown (figure) by degree of development:
questions.explanation: No official key — D primary (trophoblastic trabeculae), C secondary (mesenchymal core), A tertiary (with vessels), B mature/term.
